fichas.title: Ground source energy
fichas.summary: Overview of geothermal energy exploitation at depths up to approximately 400 m. Ground temperatures are relatively constant and can be used for heating and cooling; the page introduces horizontal ground-source collectors, downhole heat exchangers, and groundwater wells.

fichas.title: Ground source heat collectors
fichas.summary: Horizontal metal or plastic pipes installed underground collect heat for a heat pump. Their spacing and depth depend on soil properties. The page advises against building over the collectors or impermeably paving the surface.

fichas.title: Downhole heat exchangers
fichas.summary: Closed-circuit borehole heat exchangers, including U-pipe, double-pipe, and coaxial probes, provide a compact heat source for heat pumps. The borehole is grouted with cement-bentonite suspension to improve heat transfer; the diagram also shows a building-element activation arrangement for air conditioning.

fichas.title: Groundwater wells as a heat source
fichas.summary: Groundwater is extracted from an aquifer and returned through pumping or suction wells. Heat exchangers connect to a heat pump using a brine circuit. The system may require permits and approved drilling firms; the figure presents a groundwater heat source combined with underfloor heating.

fichas.title: Heat pump
fichas.summary: A heat pump uses mechanical energy to transfer environmental or geothermal heat into a heating system. Its main components are an evaporator, compressor, condenser, and expansion valve in a closed medium circuit. It can provide heating and cooling and is suited to low-temperature heating systems such as underfloor heating.

dimensions.label: Share of heating energy gained from the environment
dimensions.context: The text states that three quarters of the energy required for heating is gained from the environment; the remainder is consumed as electricity for the compressor.
